I have been farming this 5 mu piece of land for 33 years, same as my father did before me. Last year my wheat did about 450 jin per mu, and the maize after it did around 550 jin. Not the best, but not bad either. I plant what my neighbors in the village plant — if their wheat looks good, I buy the same seed from the same dealer. I don’t trust those fancy new varieties unless I see them growing in someone else’s field first.

For the wheat this autumn, I will use the same improved variety as Old Wang next door. I will spread about 100 jin of compound fertilizer per mu as base fertilizer when I sow — that is one bag. Then at green-up time in spring, I will top-dress with another 30 to 40 jin of urea per mu. I know that is maybe a bit more nitrogen than some people say I need, but last year I cut back and the wheat looked yellow and thin. I would rather spend the extra 20 yuan on fertilizer than lose a whole harvest. The wheat needs three irrigations: one before winter to help it survive the cold, one at jointing when the stems shoot up, and one at grain filling. I spray herbicide once in early spring and fungicide once if the rust shows up — that is two pesticide times. I rotary-till the field before sowing to break up the stubble.

For the summer maize, I plant right after wheat harvest in June. I use hybrid seed — everyone uses hybrid seed for maize now, you cannot get good yield without it. I put down about 80 jin of compound fertilizer per mu at sowing, then another 30 jin of urea at the big trumpet stage when the leaves are wide. The maize gets two irrigations: one at jointing/tasseling, and one at filling if the rain does not come. I spray herbicide once and insecticide once for the corn borer. I do not till for maize — I plant no-till right into the wheat stubble because there is no time to waste in summer, and the stubble keeps some moisture.

I have 7 people in my house. My son and daughter-in-law work in the factory in Handan, so they send some money home, but my wife and I do most of the farm work. Because the family has off-farm income, I can afford to buy the fertilizer I need, but I still count every yuan. Five mu is not big, but it is not small either. I have to balance everything — if fertilizer prices go up too much, I might cut the maize top dressing a little, but never the wheat base fertilizer. Wheat is my stable crop.
